question: The historical novel, 'Train to Pakistan' was written by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khushwant Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Train to Pakistan** is a historical novel authored by **Khushwant Singh**, first published in 1956.
 
• The novel vividly portrays the **Partition of India in 1947** and the associated communal violence.
 
• The story is set in the fictional village of **Mano Majra**, located near the Indo-Pak border, and focuses on the lives of its residents during the Partition.
 
• Khushwant Singh is celebrated for his sharp observations, wit, and ability to depict human emotions during turbulent times in history.
 
• The novel is considered one of the most authentic literary works capturing the human tragedy and chaos of India's Partition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khushwant Singh**

 
 
• Born on 2 February 1915, Khushwant Singh was one of India's most prominent writers, journalists, and historians.
 
• He was known for his works that explored themes of Indian history, culture, and politics with remarkable wit and candor.
 
• His other notable works include **"The Company of Women," "Delhi: A Novel,"** and **"The History of Sikhs."**
 
• He received the **Padma Vibhushan** in 2007, India's second-highest civilian award, for his contributions to literature and journalism.
 
 
 
• **Partition of India**
 
 
• The Partition of India occurred in 1947, leading to the division of British India into two independent nations: India and Pakistan.
 
• It resulted in one of the largest migrations in human history, with an estimated 10-15 million people displaced.
 
• Massive communal violence broke out, leading to the loss of countless lives, property, and social harmony.
 
 
 
• **Historical Novels**
 
 
• Historical novels are a genre of literature that reconstructs past events and settings to provide insight into history through fictional narratives.
 
• Examples of notable historical novels include **"War and Peace" by Leo Tolstoy** and **"Gone with the Wind" by Margaret Mitchell.**
